standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-quotient-henselization} and Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-quotient-strict-henselization}, cited at proof lines 11098-11099 and 11106
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the quotient of the henselization by the extended nilradical.

standard_prerequisites.name: The henselization of a reduced ring is reduced
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes that quotient reduced, giving the reverse inclusion.

core_obligations: Recall the characterisation of the nilradical as the largest nilpotent ideal with reduced quotient (proof lines 11095-11096).
Show the extended nilradical consists of nilpotent elements (proof lines 11096-11097).
Identify the quotient by the extended nilradical as the henselization of the reduced quotient and conclude it is reduced (proof lines 11098-11101).
Conclude equality and repeat the argument for the strict henselization (proof lines 11102-11107).
proof_roadmap: Nilpotence of the extended ideal (proof lines 11095-11097).
Equality and the strict case (proof lines 11102-11107).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the nilradical of the henselization and of the strict henselization with the extension of the nilradical of the local ring. The proof uses the universal property of the nilradical as the largest ideal of nilpotent elements with reduced quotient: the extended nilradical consists of nilpotent elements, and the quotient of the henselization by it is the henselization of the reduced quotient ring, hence reduced. The two facts together force the equality. The strict henselization case is handled by the analogous quotient result.
